title.exam: FIFTH SEMESTER (CUFYUGP) DEGREE EXAMINATION: MODEL PAPER 4
title.subject: PHYSICS / APPLIED PHYSICS
title.module: Module IV: Dielectric and Magnetic Properties of Solids

sections.name: Section A
sections.rule: All Questions can be answered. Each Question carries 3 marks (Ceiling: 24 Marks)
questions: Using the classical orbital picture, explain how Larmor precession produces diamagnetism. Why is the induced moment opposite to the applied field? State the approximate temperature dependence of diamagnetic susceptibility.
A paramagnetic material has $10^{28}$ atoms/m$^3$. Its susceptibility at $350\ \mathrm K$ is $2.8\times10^{-4}$. Calculate susceptibility at $300\ \mathrm K$.
What is the Néel temperature? Explain qualitatively what happens to antiferromagnetic order when a material is heated through this temperature.
Briefly explain the origin of ferrimagnetic moments.

Define electric polarisation $\mathbf P$ and electric susceptibility $\chi_e$. Write their relation to the macroscopic electric field in a linear isotropic dielectric, and state the SI unit of $\mathbf P$.
What is the local electric field at an atom? State the Lorentz local-field relation for an atomic site of cubic symmetry, and distinguish this field from the macroscopic electric field.
Define atomic polarisability and state its SI unit. Explain why polarisability is an atomic property whereas the dielectric constant is a bulk property.
Name the three principal sources of polarisability in a dielectric. Which contribution normally remains at optical frequencies, away from absorption resonances?
Discuss the ferroelectric and paraelectric states.
Explain the direct and inverse piezoelectric effects. Give one example of a piezoelectric material.

sections.name: Section B
sections.rule: All Questions can be answered. Each Question carries 6 marks (Ceiling: 36 Marks)
questions: Describe the Langevin’s theory of paramagnetism and obtain an expression for paramagnetic susceptibility. Mention the temperature dependence of susceptibility.
Derive Curie-Weiss law for ferromagnetism.

Explain the two-sublattice model of an antiferromagnet with a labelled sketch. Describe qualitatively the temperature dependence of the susceptibility parallel and perpendicular to the ordered moments below the Néel temperature, and the behaviour above it. No molecular-field algebra is required.

Explain ferrimagnetism using magnetite, $\mathrm{Fe}_3\mathrm O_4$, as an example. Describe the occupation of the two magnetic sublattices and explain which ionic moments cancel and which give the net moment. Why can the material exhibit spontaneous magnetisation and hysteresis?

For a linear isotropic dielectric, derive $\mathbf D=\varepsilon_0(1+\chi_e)\mathbf E$. A sample has $P=3.54\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{C\,m^{-2}}$ in a macroscopic field $E=2.00\times10^5\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$. Find $\chi_e$, $\varepsilon_r$ and $D$. Take $\varepsilon_0=8.85\times10^{-12}\ \mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$.
Derive the Lorentz local field $\mathbf E_{\mathrm{loc}}=\mathbf E+\mathbf P/(3\varepsilon_0)$ for an atom of cubic symmetry, explaining each term.
Describe macroscopically the origin of static dielectric constant of a substance and discuss the classical theory of electronic polarization.

Explain piezoelectricity in terms of ionic displacement under stress. Why is the absence of a centre of inversion necessary for this effect? Give an example of a crystal that is piezoelectric but not ferroelectric, and explain one practical application of the direct or inverse effect.

sections.name: Section C
sections.rule: Answer any ONE. Each Question carries 10 marks (1x10=10 Marks)
questions: Derive the Clausius–Mossotti relation $\dfrac{\varepsilon_r-1}{\varepsilon_r+2}=\dfrac{N\alpha}{3\varepsilon_0}$ from the local field. Explain the three sources of polarisability and how their contributions change with frequency.

(a) Explain spontaneous and switchable polarisation in a ferroelectric. Sketch its polarisation–electric field hysteresis loop and identify remanent polarisation and coercive field. (4 marks) (b) Explain qualitatively how the relative positions of positive and negative ions in barium titanate change across the cubic-to-tetragonal transition and produce a ferroelectric state. (4 marks) (c) Explain why a piezoelectric crystal need not be ferroelectric, using a suitable example. (2 marks)
